### Append-ready evidence units

- **R061 — 1B.** OPCW Director-General met Iran’s deputy foreign minister on 9 September 2022 and discussed cooperation concerning chemical-weapons elimination and non-re-emergence. This is target-period institutional evidence of continued treaty engagement, not proof of Khamenei’s personal direction. Contrary evidence: the meeting does not establish effective verification of all dual-use activity. Lenses: `1B.4`, `1B.6`, `1B.10`. [OPCW](https://www.opcw.org/media-centre/news/2022/09/opcw-director-general-meets-irans-deputy-foreign-minister)

- **R062 — 1B.** A February 2022 Khamenei statement publicly framed Iran’s nuclear program as needing peaceful nuclear energy and addressed ongoing negotiations. Direct attribution for doctrine and rhetoric; no evidence of command safeguards or operational orders. Lenses: `1B.2`, `1B.6`, `1B.7`. [Washington Institute](https://www.washingtoninstitute.org/policy-analysis/khamenei-breaks-his-silence-nuclear-negotiations)

- **R063 — 2B.** The UN Security Council recorded that the April–October 2022 Yemen truce reduced civilian casualties and improved fuel access and flights, while its non-renewal on 2 October ended the period of relative calm. Iran’s direct operational role remains uncertain. Contrary evidence: the truce and subsequent collapse show both a peace alternative and unresolved leverage over the Houthi side. Lenses: `2B.3`, `2B.4`, `2B.7`, `2B.9`. [UN Security Council](https://press.un.org/en/2022/sc15054.doc.htm)

- **R064 — 2B.** UNDP’s 2022 Yemen report records the negotiated truce and extension from April to October amid continuing humanitarian need. This supports a regional diplomatic alternative but does not attribute the outcome personally to Khamenei. Lenses: `2B.3`, `2B.7`, `2B.9`. [UNDP](https://www.undp.org/yemen/publications/peace-support-facility-yemen-2022-annual-report)

- **R065 — 3B.** Amnesty’s April 2022 prison-health investigation documented 96 custody-death cases and described rules allowing prison directors and prosecution officials to override medical advice concerning hospital transfers. Persistent conditions remained relevant during 2022. Attribution is to prison/prosecution institutions, not Khamenei personally. Lenses: `3B.2`, `3B.4`, `3B.6`, `3B.9`. [Amnesty International](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2022/04/iran-ailing-prisoners-left-to-die-amid-crisis-of-impunity-for-fatal-denial-of-medical-care/)

- **R066 — 3B.** The UN Human Rights Council’s November 2022 resolution created an independent fact-finding mission, required evidence preservation, and called on Iran to provide access and information. Contrary evidence: the resolution records an institutional accountability response, not a completed domestic remedy; later reporting indicated Iran had not provided access. Lenses: `3B.4`, `3B.9`, `3B.10`. [UN Geneva](https://www.ungeneva.org/en/news-media/meeting-summary/2022/11/afternoon-human-rights-council-establishes-fact-finding-mission)

- **R067 — 3B.** In October 2022, judiciary chief Mohseni Ejei publicly referred to governmental “mistakes, weaknesses and failures” and expressed openness to dialogue and criticism. This is contrary remedial rhetoric, not evidence of investigation, correction, or accountability. Lenses: `3B.7`, `3B.9`, `3B.10`. [TIME](https://time.com/6221004/iran-protests-mahsa-amini-change/)

- **R068 — 4B.** November 2022 reporting documented clerics and reformist politicians demanding a constitutional referendum, while some officials pursued dialogue with protesting students. This provides evidence of internal contestation and institutional resistance. Contrary evidence: the security crackdown continued and senior leaders resisted structural reform. Lenses: `4B.4`, `4B.8`, `4B.10`. [The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/nov/08/iranian-leaders-resist-growing-demands-on-referendum-on-constitution)

- **R069 — 4B.** On 6 December 2022, Iran’s legislative and executive leaders rejected calls for constitutional change despite nationwide protests. This is a precise target-period governance event showing institutional closure after contestation. Attribution is shared institutional leadership, not solely Khamenei. Lenses: `4B.4`, `4B.7`, `4B.8`, `4B.10`. [ConstitutionNet](https://constitutionnet.org/news/iran-lawmakers-reject-popular-calls-constitutional-reform-response-protests)

- **R070 — 5B.** A peer-reviewed September 2022 study found Iran’s subsidy/cash-transfer policy had heterogeneous effects by income, geography, energy consumption, and transfer share; inflation eroded gains. This adds household-distribution evidence while preserving policy-system attribution. Lenses: `5B.5`, `5B.6`, `5B.8`, `5B.10`. [Energy Policy](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301421522003706)

- **R071 — 5B.** Contemporary reporting linked the May–June 2022 food-price protests to subsidy removal, drought, sanctions, inflation, corruption, and government mismanagement. This records household exposure and implementation controversy, not a personal Khamenei finding. Lenses: `5B.2`, `5B.5`, `5B.6`, `5B.10`. [USIP](https://iranprimer.usip.org/blog/2022/jun/01/explainer-iran-protests-over-food-prices)

- **R072 — 6B.** UNHCR reported that in 2022 it funded universal public health-insurance premiums for up to 120,000 vulnerable refugees, with coverage through Iran’s national health-insurance system. Attribution is UNHCR/Iranian health-system implementation, not Khamenei. Contrary evidence: access depended on external funding and vulnerable groups remained exposed to sanctions and capacity constraints. Lenses: `6B.1`, `6B.3`, `6B.5`, `6B.8`. [UNHCR](https://www.unhcr.org/ir/health-insurance-refugees-0)

- **R073 — 6B.** UNICEF reported 2022 cooperation with Iran’s Ministry of Education to finance and equip school-entry health screening for Afghan refugee, nomad, and disadvantaged children in several provinces. This is bounded service delivery and equity evidence, not ruler-attributed management. Lenses: `6B.1`, `6B.3`, `6B.5`, `6B.8`. [UNICEF](https://www.unicef.org/iran/en/press-releases/unicef-supports-school-entrance-health-screening-15-million-children-iran)

- **R074 — 7B.** Iran Open Data’s review of the 2022 appropriations bill reported that Supreme-Leader-linked foundations and institutions paid a very small share of national tax receipts and controlled significant economic activity. This supports an institutional-transparency concern, not personal enrichment. Lenses: `7B.2`, `7B.3`, `7B.5`, `7B.8`. [Iran Open Data](https://iranopendata.org/en/article/the-unpaid-taxes-of-supreme-leader-affiliated-foundations-and-institutions/)

- **R075 — 7B.** Freedom House’s 2022 assessment found IRGC and bonyad economic actors were effectively above scrutiny and that journalists and civil society lacked the capacity to provide independent oversight. Contrary evidence: no verified personal asset or enrichment finding against Khamenei was recovered. Lenses: `7B.3`, `7B.5`, `7B.6`, `7B.9`. [Freedom House](https://freedomhouse.org/country/iran/freedom-world/2022)

- **R076 — 8B.** UNICEF reported that in 2022 its cooperation with Iran supported school-entry health screening for approximately 1.5 million children, including refugee, nomad, and disadvantaged children, and equipped Ministry of Education screening centers with 545 laptops. This is a bounded implementation success with measurable reach; attribution remains UNICEF/ministry-level. Lenses: `8B.3`, `8B.5`, `8B.7`, `8B.9`. [UNICEF](https://www.unicef.org/iran/en/press-releases/unicef-supports-school-entrance-health-screening-15-million-children-iran)

### Continuation assessment

The searches materially improved:

- 1B dual-use treaty-engagement and doctrine coverage;
- 2B peace alternatives and Yemen-truce evidence;
- 3B routine prison conditions and limited remedial rhetoric;
- 4B institutional contestation and reform resistance;
- 5B household distributional effects;
- 6B refugee and disadvantaged-child service delivery;
- 7B institutional transparency and auditability;
- 8B measurable partner-supported implementation.

The principal gaps remain unresolved:

- Khamenei’s personal operational control over nuclear, proxy, economic, and welfare decisions;
- command-and-control safeguards and crisis procedures;
- verified personal assets, enrichment, procurement, or court findings;
- independent monitoring of budgets, appointments, milestones, adaptation, and correction;
- closed-system underreporting and missing domestic records.
